86: + * as a name, not dressed up as content.

91: +import type { ChatAttachment } from "../types";
92: +
93: +/** How much of a text file the model sees. */
94: +export const MAX_ATTACHMENT_CHARS = 20_000;

96: +/** A single image, bounded so a data URL cannot bloat the request. */
97: +export const MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;

99: +export const ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT = [
100: +  "text/*",
101: +  ".md",
102: +  ".mdx",
103: +  ".json",
104: +  ".csv",
105: +  ".yaml",
106: +  ".yml",
107: +  ".log",
108: +  "image/png",
109: +  "image/jpeg",
110: +  "image/webp",
111: +  "image/gif",
112: +].join(",");
113: +
114: +const TEXT_LIKE = /^(text\/|application\/(json|yaml|x-yaml)$)/;
115: +const SUPPORTED_IMAGE_TYPES = new Set(
116: +  ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT.split(",").filter((type) => type.startsWith("image/")),
117: +);
118: +
119: +export function isTextLike(name: string, contentType: string): boolean {
120: +  if (TEXT_LIKE.test(contentType)) {
121: +    return true;
122: +  }
123: +  return /\.(md|mdx|json|csv|ya?ml|txt|log)$/i.test(name);
124: +}
125: +
126: +export function isImageLike(contentType: string): boolean {
127: +  return contentType.startsWith("image/");
128: +}
129: +
130: +/**
131: + * Why a dropped or pasted file cannot become an attachment, or null if it can.
132: + *
133: + * The file input already honours `accept`; a drop bypasses it, so the same
134: + * rule is applied here rather than letting an unreadable file become a chip
135: + * that promises content the model will never see.
136: + */
137: +export function attachmentRejection(file: File): string | null {
138: +  if (isImageLike(file.type)) {
139: +    if (!SUPPORTED_IMAGE_TYPES.has(file.type)) {
140: +      return `${file.name} is not an image the studio can read (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF).`;
141: +    }
142: +    if (file.size > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES) {
143: +      return `${file.name} is larger than ${Math.floor(MAX_IMAGE_BYTES / (1024 * 1024))} MB.`;
144: +    }
145: +    return null;
146: +  }
147: +  if (isTextLike(file.name, file.type)) {
148: +    return null;
149: +  }
150: +  return `${file.name} is not a text or image file the studio can read.`;
151: +}
152: +
153: +/** A short size for an attachment chip; empty when there is nothing to say. */
154: +export function formatFileSize(bytes: number): string {
155: +  if (!bytes || bytes < 0) {
156: +    return "";
157: +  }
158: +  if (bytes < 1024) {
159: +    return `${bytes} B`;
160: +  }
161: +  if (bytes < 1024 * 1024) {
162: +    return `${Math.round(bytes / 1024)} KB`;
163: +  }
164: +  return `${(bytes / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(1)} MB`;
165: +}

167: +function readAsDataUrl(file: File): Promise<string> {
168: +  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
169: +    const reader = new FileReader();
170: +    reader.onload = () => resolve(String(reader.result ?? ""));
171: +    reader.onerror = () => reject(reader.error ?? new Error("Could not read the file."));

173: +  });
174: +}

176: +/**
177: + * Prepare one file for a turn. Never throws: an unreadable file becomes a
178: + * name-only attachment so the user can still see what they attached.
179: + */
180: +export async function prepareAttachment(file: File): Promise<ChatAttachment> {
181: +  const base: ChatAttachment = {
182: +    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
183: +    name: file.name,
184: +    contentType: file.type || "application/octet-stream",
185: +    size: file.size,
186: +  };
187: +
188: +  try {
189: +    if (isImageLike(base.contentType) && file.size <= MAX_IMAGE_BYTES) {
190: +      return { ...base, dataUrl: await readAsDataUrl(file) };
191: +    }
192: +    if (isTextLike(file.name, base.contentType)) {
193: +      const text = await file.text();
194: +      return { ...base, text: text.slice(0, MAX_ATTACHMENT_CHARS) };
195: +    }
196: +  } catch {

198: +  }
199: +
200: +  return base;
201: +}

223: +

226: +    },

229: +      const file = attachment.file;
230: +      const ready = file

232: +        : {
233: +            id: attachment.id,
234: +            name: attachment.name,
235: +            contentType: attachment.contentType ?? "application/octet-stream",
236: +            size: 0,
237: +          };
238: +      ATTACHMENTS.set(attachment.id, ready);
239: +      return {
240: +        ...attachment,
241: +        status: { type: "complete" },
242: +        content: [
243: +          {
244: +            type: "file",
245: +            data: attachment.id,
246: +            mimeType: ready.contentType,
247: +            filename: ready.name,
248: +          },
249: +        ],
250: +      };
251: +    },
252: +  };
253: +}
254: +
255: +/** Process-wide, because the runtime adapter outlives a render. */
256: +const ATTACHMENTS = new Map<string, ChatAttachment>();
257: +
258: +/** The extraction for one attachment, for showing what was actually sent. */
259: +export function preparedAttachmentById(id: string): ChatAttachment | undefined {
